subject: maths
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Co-interior (allied) angles between parallel lines: one is 130°. What is the other?
questions.explain: Co-interior angles sum to 180°, so 180° − 130° = 50°.

questions.q: An exterior angle of a regular polygon is 40°. How many sides does it have?
questions.explain: Number of sides = 360° ÷ 40° = 9.

questions.q: Two angles are vertically opposite. One is 47°. What is the other?
questions.explain: Vertically opposite angles are equal, so it is 47°.

questions.q: Two angles lie on a straight line. One is 110°. What is the other?
questions.explain: Angles on a straight line sum to 180°, so 180° − 110° = 70°.

questions.q: An equilateral triangle has all sides equal. What is the size of each interior angle?
questions.explain: Angles sum to 180 deg and all three are equal, so each is 180 / 3 = 60 deg.

questions.q: The bearing of B from A is 070°. What is the bearing of A from B?
questions.explain: A back bearing adds 180°, so 070° + 180° = 250°.

questions.q: The angle in a semicircle (in the triangle on a diameter) is always:
questions.explain: By the circle theorem, the angle in a semicircle is a right angle, 90 deg.

questions.q: Three angles meet at a point and are 120°, 150° and x. What is x?
questions.explain: Angles around a point sum to 360°, so x = 360° − 120° − 150° = 90°.

questions.q: What is the sum of the interior angles of a hexagon?
An exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles. If those are 50 deg and 60 deg, what is the exterior angle?
questions.explain: Exterior angle = 50 + 60 = 110 deg.

questions.q: Each interior angle of a regular polygon is 150 deg. How many sides does it have?
questions.explain: Each exterior angle = 180 - 150 = 30 deg, so sides = 360 / 30 = 12.

questions.q: An isosceles triangle has an apex angle of 40°. What is each base angle?
questions.explain: The two equal base angles share 180° − 40° = 140°, so each is 70°.

questions.q: Three angles of a quadrilateral are 90°, 100° and 80°. What is the fourth angle?
questions.explain: Angles in a quadrilateral sum to 360°, so 360° − 90° − 100° − 80° = 90°.

questions.q: Two parallel lines are crossed by a transversal. One angle is 75°. What is its alternate angle?
questions.explain: Alternate (Z) angles between parallel lines are equal, so it is 75°.

questions.q: Two parallel lines are crossed by a transversal. One angle is 112 deg. What is its corresponding angle?
questions.explain: Corresponding (F) angles are equal, so it is 112 deg.

questions.q: Two triangles are similar with a scale factor of 3. A side of 4 cm on the small triangle matches which side on the large one?
questions.explain: Multiply by the scale factor: 4 x 3 = 12 cm.

questions.q: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
questions.explain: A square has 4 lines of symmetry.

questions.q: A line drawn from the centre of a circle to a point on the circumference is called the:
questions.explain: A radius joins the centre to the circumference.

questions.q: A triangle has angles in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3. What is the largest angle?
questions.explain: Total parts = 6, each part = 180 / 6 = 30 deg, so the largest is 3 x 30 = 90 deg.

questions.q: Two angles in a triangle are 55° and 65°. What is the third angle?
questions.explain: Angles in a triangle sum to 180°, so 180° − 55° − 65° = 60°.

questions.q: How many degrees does each interior angle of a regular pentagon measure?
questions.explain: Interior sum = (5 - 2) x 180 = 540 deg, and 540 / 5 = 108 deg.

questions.q: In a parallelogram, one angle is 70 deg. What is the size of an adjacent angle?
questions.explain: Adjacent angles in a parallelogram are co-interior and sum to 180 deg, so 180 - 70 = 110 deg.
